title: Time 6: Mixed Review (pin any event in time)
description: Bring the whole track together: Который час and час/часа/часов; в + accusative for clock times and days; the genitive for dates; через ... and ... назад; по + dative for recurring days and the bare instrumental for parts of the day. Choose the right preposition and case for each kind of time phrase.
descriptionRussian: Сводим весь трек воедино: Который час и час/часа/часов; в + винительный для времени по часам и дней; родительный для дат; через… и …назад; по + дательный для повторяющихся дней и чистый творительный для частей суток. Выбирайте правильный предлог и падеж для каждого типа выражения времени.
intro: Pinning an event in time turns out to need five different patterns, and which one you use depends only on what kind of time it is. A clock time and a single day share a preposition. A date takes none. Forward and backward distances take their own words. Recurring days take another. Identify the kind of time first.
rules: Clock count: 1 → час, 2-4 → часа, 5+ → часов. Ask with Который час?
в + accusative for clock times and single days: в два часа, в пять часов, в понедельник, в среду (feminine -а → -у), во вторник.
Dates take the bare genitive, no preposition: первого мая, пятого марта. The date itself is a nominative ordinal: Сегодня первое мая. Years: в ... году.
через ... before for the future, ... назад after for the past; the time word is accusative: через неделю, неделю назад.
по + dative plural for recurring days (по понедельникам); bare instrumental for parts of the day (утром, вечером); каждый + accusative for 'every' (каждый день).
examples: Сейчас четыре часа. (It is four o'clock.) clock count: 4 → часа.
Урок в два часа. (The lesson is at two o'clock.) в + accusative for the clock time.
Концерт первого мая. (The concert is on the first of May.) date, bare genitive.
Я приду через час. (I will come in an hour.) через before, future.
Он ушёл неделю назад. (He left a week ago.) назад after, past.
По субботам я отдыхаю, а утром пью кофе. (On Saturdays I rest, and in the mornings I drink coffee.) по + dative plural and bare instrumental together.

tables.title: The five time patterns at a glance

rows.label: At a time / on a day

items.hint: 5 is in the '5 and up' group.
items.explanation: 5 takes часов: пять часов. The forms час (after 1) and часа (after 2-4) would be wrong here.

items.promptEnglish: The concert will be on the first of May.
items.hint: On a date: genitive ordinal, no preposition.
items.explanation: On a date the ordinal is in the genitive with no preposition: первого мая. The nominative первое мая is for the date itself ('today is the first of May').

items.promptEnglish: I will come in an hour.
items.hint: Looking forward to the future; the word goes before the time.
items.explanation: Future distance uses через before the time: через час. Назад ('ago') would point to the past and would follow the time.

items.hint: A weekly routine, not one specific Monday.
items.explanation: Recurring days use по + dative plural: по понедельникам. В понедельник would mean one specific Monday.

items.prompt: _____ я пью кофе, а вечером чай.
items.promptEnglish: In the morning I drink coffee, and in the evening tea.
items.hint: A part of the day, paired with вечером later in the sentence.
items.explanation: Parts of the day use the bare instrumental: утром (matching вечером). No preposition is needed.

items.promptEnglish: The lesson starts at two o'clock.
items.hint: в + the plain counting number; час is masculine.
items.explanation: 'At two o'clock' is в два часа: the number два (masculine, with час) plus часа for the 2-4 group.

blanks: Мы приехали неделю _____. (We arrived a week ago.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Past distance uses назад after the accusative time phrase: неделю назад. Через would mean 'in a week' (future) and would come before the time.

categorySorting.instruction: Sort each time phrase by the pattern it uses.

errorCorrection.sentence: Каждый день я встаю в семь часах.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Every day I get up at seven o'clock.
errorCorrection.explanation: For a clock time Russian uses в + accusative, and after 7 the noun takes часов (the 5-and-up counting form): в семь часов. Часах is the prepositional, which English speakers reach for because в often pairs with the prepositional for location, but a clock time uses в + accusative. The correct phrase is в семь часов.

errorCorrection.translationEnglish: The concert will be on the second of May.
errorCorrection.explanation: To say something happens ON a date, the day-ordinal goes into the genitive -ого with no preposition: второго мая. Второе is the nominative, right for stating the date itself (Сегодня второе мая).

For a recurring day ('on Mondays', every Monday) Russian uses по + the dative plural: по понедельникам. The noun понедельникам is already the dative plural, so only the preposition is wrong: в marks one specific day with the accusative (в понедельник - on Monday), not a routine. The correct phrase is по понедельникам.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I was born on the first of May.
minimalPairs.explanation: Dates take the bare genitive with no preposition: первого мая. Adding в is the typical mistake; dates simply do not use в.

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: On Wednesdays I go to the pool.
minimalPairs.explanation: A weekly routine ('on Wednesdays') is по средам, with по + dative plural. В среду would mean one specific Wednesday.

reviewVocab.definition: the default for 'at a clock time' and 'on a single day': в два часа, в пять часов, в понедельник, в среду.
reviewVocab.example: Урок в два часа в среду.

reviewVocab.term: родительный для дат / через и назад
reviewVocab.definition: dates use the bare genitive (первого мая); future and past distance use через before and назад after (через час, час назад).
reviewVocab.example: Концерт первого мая, а экзамен через неделю.

reviewVocab.definition: recurring days take по + dative plural (по понедельникам); parts of the day take the bare instrumental (утром, вечером).
reviewVocab.example: По субботам я отдыхаю, а утром пью кофе.
